observation.visible_scene: A close-up shot of a clear glass mixing bowl resting on a white surface, with a black-and-white striped cloth visible under its left side. Inside the bowl is a brown, glossy liquid batter. A metal balloon whisk is held in the mixture and is being moved in a circular stirring motion throughout the clip. A 'J / Dessert' watermark sits in the top-right corner. The bowl rim, cloth, whisk, and batter remain present in every frame.
visible_changes: The whisk continuously rotates and sweeps around the bowl; in some frames its wires are sharply visible (e.g. frames 1, 5, 10, 17, 26, 30, 34, 38, 40) while in others it is motion-blurred into a pale streak (e.g. frames 2, 4, 6, 9, 11, 14, 16, 18, 21, 25, 27, 29, 31, 33, 35, 37, 39, 41), indicating fast movement rather than a different tool.
The surface of the batter shows evolving concentric ripples and swirling trails that shift position as the whisk passes, demonstrating ongoing deformation of the liquid from the stirring.

The batter's appearance transitions from a lighter pinkish-brown with uneven tone in the early frames to a more uniform, smooth, glossy chocolate-brown in the later frames, consistent with continued mixing.

The whisk's working end moves between the right side, center, and left-center of the bowl over the sequence, tracking a circular path; the bowl and cloth stay largely fixed in frame, so the dominant motion is the whisk and the liquid, not the camera.
The stirring is already in progress at the first sampled frame and is still in progress at the last; no start or stop of the action is captured.
outside_clip_unknowns: What ingredients were added or combined before this segment began.
The final texture or use of the batter after the clip ends.
Whether the color change reflects true mixing/incorporation or exposure/lighting variation, since no separate ingredient addition is visible.
uncertain_details: Minor apparent framing shifts (the bowl's left rim and the cloth occupy slightly different portions of the image across frames) could be a small camera move or a slight repositioning of the bowl; background evidence is insufficient to confirm camera motion.
The cause of the batter darkening/smoothing is not directly observable; only the visual change is supported.
Individual whisk strokes cannot be counted reliably because of motion blur in many frames.
